key_insight: In a ducted turbulent aeroacoustic flow, changing the spacing between two orifices can metamorphose the onset of limit-cycle oscillations from continuous to abrupt, with a canard explosion mediating the transition.
engineering_relevance: This reveals a controllable route to oscillatory instability in aeroacoustic systems, supporting low-cost design and mitigation strategies for noise and instability control.
method: Conducted experiments on ducted turbulent flow with two orifices separated by varying distances.
Varied Reynolds number as the bifurcation parameter driving transitions between limit cycles.
Used the orifice spacing as a secondary parameter to observe changes in transition criticality.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental observation of two distinct abrupt bifurcations, including a continuous-to-abrupt metamorphosis through a canard explosion.
watch_item: The findings are based on a specific ducted aeroacoustic configuration, so the transition types and control implications may not generalize without validation in other geometries and flow conditions.
paper_title: Metamorphosis of transition between states of limit cycle oscillations in aeroacoustic system
